title: Describe a crash
description:
A crash reporter receives an exception code and, for access violations, two more facts: the kind of access (0 read, 1 write, 8 execute) and the address. Write `describe(code, access, address)`, which returns a one-line summary:

| Code | Summary |
|---|---|
| `0xC0000005` | `"access violation reading 0x..."`, `"writing 0x..."` or `"executing 0x..."` with the address in upper-case hex, followed by `" (null pointer)"` if the address is below `0x10000` |
| `0xC00000FD` | `"stack overflow"` |
| `0xC0000094` | `"integer divide by zero"` |
| `0xC0000409` | `"stack buffer overrun"` |
| `0xE06D7363` | `"unhandled C++ exception"` |
| anything else | `"exception 0x..."` with the code as 8 upper-case hex digits |

`access` and `address` are only used for access violations.

```
describe(0xC0000005, 0, 0x10)              = "access violation reading 0x10 (null pointer)"
describe(0xC0000005, 1, 0x7FF6A1230000)    = "access violation writing 0x7FF6A1230000"
describe(0x80000003, 0, 0)                 = "exception 0x80000003"
```
hints: A `switch` on the code handles the named cases. `std::format("{:X}", n)` writes upper-case hex; `{:08X}` pads to 8 digits.
The first 64 KB of the address space is never mapped (lesson 6.02), so an address below `0x10000` almost always means a null pointer plus an offset.
